title: PSG2-QSTORE: clean Dense with a measured basis store

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single physical PSG2-QSTORE algorithm in grover_quantum_storage.md and all seven required appendices in its evidence list simulates the complete virtual Dense P with the specified fixed-region measured basis-qubit controller, source/weighted cutoffs and output-first cleanup. It recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 from independent ideal source copies. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, rejected/discarded copies, numerical errors, failures, aborts, initialization and cleanup, its total charged sequential work obeys T(N,s)=O(2^((177/250)sqrt(n log2 n))). The complete representative envelope is B_T(n)=2^((177/250)sqrt(n log2 n)), for n>=2 with the explicit finite virtual branch and same interpreter covering n=1. Its exact growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes. This bound holds jointly with the other three physical resource bounds and the zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration. All source resource assertions in the six virtual appendices refer to virtual P, not to the physical classical allocation.

For the same physical PSG2-QSTORE algorithm and complete parameter/controller rule in grover_quantum_storage.md and all seven required appendices in its evidence list, the proved malformed-copy fractional guarantee is epsilon(n)=0: all Q actual acquired copies are independent ideal coset states. For every N>=2 and every s, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 jointly with the four every-branch physical resource bounds. The same simulator executes the virtual finite branch at n=1. No positive malformed-copy or adaptive-source transfer is claimed, and this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
